thesis: Hold a river out of training and the preprint's AI still counted Alaska's big rivers closely (Kenai banks under 7 and 3 percent, Nushagak about 3.5 percent) while a small California river broke (0.33 to 0.80), so what the preprint leaves open is not the held-out test but use in the field.
supporting_facts: c15 Kenai bank misses under 0.07 and 0.03 across all training conditions including held out (0.069, 0.025), direction near zero
c23 Kenai-Channel doubled when held out, 0.143 to 0.286
c18 Mad River 0.33 to 0.80 held out, a California river whose fish the preprint calls small and sparse
c19 built for deployment, no agency use reported
counterpoint_honored: The Kenai channel site doubled when held out, three California rivers broke, the benchmark is one team's offline preprint, and the informal 10 percent human figure is a different ruler. Alaska's strong held-out numbers are a result on recorded video, not use in the field.
falsifiable: False if the held-out Alaska values were as large as the California ones, or if the preprint reported an agency using it.
runner_ups: upside-only: home-water win (boosterish, hides the held-out test)
volume-hook only: 855,936 in a day (kept as the cold open, not the thesis)
cross_challenge: All three analysts converged. Challenges applied: never say beats humans (0.07/0.03 vs informal 10 percent are different measures); Mad River always tagged California and small-count; no cause for any error; no ADF&G AI use; Nushagak -0.65 cut.
correction_2026-10-28: An earlier draft said the preprint reports no held-out Alaska number. Table 7 (OOD column) does report one for every Alaska site, and they are low except the Kenai channel. The film was rebuilt on the verified table.
